title: Cell Overvoltage / Undervoltage Hazard

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Synthetic hazard analysis for hypothetical automotive BMS project

malfunctioning_behavior: AFE reports incorrect cell voltage (stuck-at, drift, communication error) OR SOA fails to detect limit violation OR contactor fails to open on violation OR BMS fails to request contactor opening

hazardous_events.description: Cell overvoltage during charging leading to thermal runaway
hazardous_events.operational_situation: CHARGING mode, high SOC (>90%), fast charge (>1C), ambient > 45°C
hazardous_events.rationale: Thermal runaway can cause fire/explosion with fatal injuries; continuous exposure during charging; driver cannot detect or control individual cell overvoltage

hazardous_events.description: Cell undervoltage during discharge leading to copper shunts and potential thermal event on subsequent recharge
hazardous_events.operational_situation: NORMAL mode, deep discharge (<2.0V/cell), high load, low temperature
hazardous_events.rationale: Cell damage creates latent failure; moderate exposure during deep discharge; vehicle may provide warning but driver may ignore

safe_states: All HV contactors open (HV bus isolated from pack)
Fault logged to FRAM with timestamp and cell index
degraded_states: Balancing disabled for affected cell group
Enhanced monitoring: 1 Hz acquisition for affected cells
assumptions: Vehicle provides independent HW monitoring (e.g., redundant voltage monitor ASIL B)
Charger respects BMS charge current limits
Contactor opening is irreversible without service tool
FRAM retains fault data across power cycles
